record.title: OpenAI releases a claimed AI-generated refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis with Lean formalization
record.summary: OpenAI reports that an internal model produced a refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), then released a natural-language manuscript and Lean formalization. The linked Lean scope describes a subexponential exact-counting bound for fixed-k canonical k-CNF formulas, a formalized statement that would contradict ETH if its definitions and scope match the standard conjecture. OpenAI says an external group led by Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi and Ryan Williams will examine the result; the group’s participation is not certification. Independent mathematical review, a reproduced build and practical algorithmic consequences remain unestablished.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: On October 26, OpenAI published an announcement describing an AI-generated ETH refutation and linked a natural-language manuscript and Lean formalization in its public repository.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI reports that its system produced a refutation of ETH. The linked Lean scope states that, for each fixed k at least 2, a deterministic machine exactly counts satisfying assignments of canonical k-CNF formulas in subexponential time with polynomial space; the manuscript states a sharper exponent for m clauses. Correctness and correspondence to the standard ETH formulation have not been independently established here.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI says an external group led by Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi and Ryan Williams will examine the result and that the group requested public raw materials; their participation does not certify the claim.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: No independent mathematical conclusion, independent Lean build, or practical algorithmic speedup is established by the sources inspected in this activation.

evidence_gaps.description: The proof has not been independently reviewed or built from a pinned repository revision in this activation; formal correctness and correspondence between formal and informal statements remain open.
The reported subexponential counting bound does not establish a practical speedup on real instances or polynomial-time solvability.

brief.importance_rationale: If the bounded theorem genuinely refutes ETH for standard exact k-SAT, many conditional lower-bound arguments across theoretical computer science would require reassessment. The score reflects consequence if true; independent proof review and practical algorithmic impact are not established.
limitations: The theorem remains an OpenAI-reported claim; independent correctness and standard-ETH correspondence are not established.
The GitHub scope document was read from a mutable main branch and was not pinned or independently built.
Subexponential time is not polynomial time; the announcement does not establish P = NP or practical speedups.
The external group's involvement is explicitly not certification; the result awaits independent examination.

technical.claimed_result: OpenAI reports a Lean-formalized, subexponential exact-counting result for fixed-k canonical k-CNF, which would contradict ETH if its statement and scope match the standard conjecture.
technical.demonstrated_result: The Oct 26 release and linked formalization-scope page are directly observable; theorem correctness and independent formal build were not established.
technical.mechanism: The linked scope describes deterministic exact counting in subexponential time with polynomial space and links a Lean theorem named SubexponentialSAT.lean. The full proof and dependencies were not built or analyzed in this activation.
technical.regime: Fixed k≥2 canonical k-CNF; the scope page states an exponent O_k(n(log log n)^2/sqrt(log n)) plus polynomial encoding-length factors, and polynomial space.
technical.reproducibility: Public natural-language and Lean artifacts are linked from OpenAI’s announcement. Repository state was mutable main; no commit pin, build, or independent verification was performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: Not applicable to the source-reported theorem claim; no algorithmic benchmark comparison was inspected.

brief.title: OpenAI releases a claimed AI-generated refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis with Lean formalization
brief.why_it_matters: If the formalized and manuscript claims are correct and match standard ETH, complexity results that rely on ETH would need reassessment. A subexponential exact algorithm would not by itself establish polynomial-time solvability or settle P versus NP.
